transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-08-25 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48m 12s
Attendees: Maya R (Redwood AE), Liam C (Redwood SE), Priya N (Redwood Product), Samir P (Vento Head AI), Jenna M (Product), Evan L (ML Eng), Tara S (Security)

Summary: Quick EvalOps lab to show prompt set management, regression alerting, and A/B comparison flows in the Console and a bit of the API. Customer wants to validate regression detection on clinical triage assistant responses and compare two candidate model configs (quantized LLM vs a superfine-tuned smaller model).

Topics: prompt set creation, ground truth labeling, drift/regression alerts thresholds, A/B split traffic, cost estimates, hosting (hosted vs VPC), SOC2 / KMS questions.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody thanks for joining, um quick roll call?
[00:05] Jenna: Jenna here, Samir?
[00:07] Samir: Samir on, Evan here too.
[00:09] Evan: yep
[00:10] Tara: Tara from security.
[00:12] Maya: Great, so we planned a 45 minute lab, we'll go through Console demo, then API snippet and finish with next steps. Liam you'll lead the prompt set part?
[00:20] Liam: Yeah I'll walk the console, show prompt set creation, uploading CSVs, the idea of seed labels and then how alerts fire.
[00:26] Priya: I'll jump in on the A/B compare UI - how we configure population splits and success metrics.
[00:30] Samir: High level: we want to catch regressions where the triage assistant starts missing red flags for chest pain triage. Need high recall. Also timeline: pilot in Sept, production in Q4 if pilot good.
[00:45] Maya: Good, that timeline makes sense. Quick qual: are you leaning hosted Redwood API or on-prem/VPC?
[00:53] Jenna: We prefer hosted for speed but security wants to look at data residency and KMS before deciding.
[00:58] Tara: correct, we need SOC2+, and then if we see anything sensitive we may ask for private deployment. KMS/HSM integration is important.
[01:10] Liam: Noted. In the Console demo you'll see we can tie audit logs to your SIEM and we have KMS integrations for private deployments, or in hosted we support customer-managed keys for object storage.
[01:25] Liam: Ok, let's jump to Console - I'm sharing my screen. (short pause) Loading EvalOps -> Prompt Sets.
[01:36] Liam: Here's a sample prompt set: columns are id, prompt_text, expected_label, notes. You can import via CSV or paste. Notice we can tag prompts by scenario: chest_pain, medication_interaction, red_flag.
[01:50] Jenna: How many prompts do we need to start catching regressions?
[01:53] Liam: Good q. For signal you can start with 500-1k targeted prompts across critical flows. For baseline regression detection we recommend 2-4k over diverse examples, but the seed set depends on variability.
[02:05] Evan: Does the system support fuzzy matching for paraphrase? Our users write a lot of variants.
[02:08] Liam: Yes - the scoring supports both exact match and semantic similarity using embeddings. We calculate a similarity score and you can set thresholds. Note: embeddings cost are extra but low compared to generation.
[02:20] Samir: Cool. Show us how an alert looks when a regression triggers.
[02:23] Liam: Sure. I'll simulate a batch run - run eval -> compare to baseline. (keyboard clack) This run is synthetic but demonstrates a regression where recall drops 7% for chest_pain.
[02:40] [00:02:40] Speaker 2: oh that's the alarm icon, you can set severity levels, email + webhook.
[02:47] Priya: The alert has a triage playbook link so you can attach runbooks and assign to an on-call.
[02:55] Jenna: Can we get a digest for product managers and a separate one for infra?
[02:58] Liam: Yep, alert routing by tag or team - e.g., a security-tagged regression goes to security.
[03:05] Evan: For A/B, do you do live traffic splits or offline compare?
[03:08] Priya: Both. You can do offline A/B comparisons on historical logs or live split with traffic routing. For live A/B you can pick percent splits and rollout schedules and auto-fallback if error rate spikes.
[03:20] Samir: For live we want canary then broader rollout, and fallback to the baseline model if quality dips.
[03:25] Maya: Redwood supports automatic fallback policies and model variant routing in the serving layer, yes.
[03:30] Tara: In live splits, do you capture PII? How is logs retention handled?
[03:35] Liam: By default we redact high confidence PII in the hosted offering and provide retention windows; for strict retention you can run Private where logs stay in your VPC and we can configure minimal retention.
[03:46] Jenna: Are embeddings stored? We don't want patient identifiers stuck in vector stores.
[03:50] Liam: We recommend hashing sensitive tokens and using ephemeral embeddings or encrypted stores behind your KMS. We'll share an architecture note.
[04:00] [00:04:00] Speaker 1: ok demo time for A/B compare - I'm switching to the A/B tab.
[04:07] Priya: Here we create a comparison: Candidate A = quantized 13B with extra prompt engineering, Candidate B = fine-tuned 7B. We select metric: recall_on_red_flags and a macro-f1.
[04:20] Jenna: Can we set custom metrics? Our product team uses a weighted metric to prioritize recall by 3x over precision.
[04:25] Priya: Yes - you can supply a custom scoring function or weight existing metrics. The UI also allows composite metrics.
[04:33] Evan: How reproducible are runs? We need deterministic seeds for sampling.
[04:36] Liam: Runs are logged with model version, tokenization, seed, and hardware profile. You can export run artifacts.
[04:44] Samir: Let's talk scale and cost - if we run a daily regression test of 10k prompts, whats the token cost?
[04:50] Liam: Rough estimate depends on model. For a 13B quantized model at median prompt length ~60 tokens and generation ~40 tokens, you're looking ~1.1M tokens per daily run. We'll attach a cost example but ballpark $X/day depending on plan and discounts.
[05:08] Samir: We need the exact spreadsheet for budgeting.
[05:10] Maya: I'll send a sample benchmark/spreadsheet.
[05:12] Jenna: On the API side - can we programmatically create prompt sets and trigger runs?
[05:15] Liam: Yes - there's an EvalOps REST API. Example: POST /evals/prompt-sets with CSV or JSON, then POST /evals/run. We also have SDKs.
[05:25] Evan: Do we get streaming progress?
[05:27] Liam: You can stream eval progress and partial results via webhooks or a streaming websocket.
[05:33] [00:05:33] Speaker 3: question from Samir - how do we handle ground truth labeling at scale?
[05:36] Priya: We integrate with third-party label tools and also have a lightweight label UI for quick adjudication. You can upload gold labels and use crowd/annotator links.
[05:45] Samir: For chest pain we have clinician labels - can we lock those as ground truth?
[05:48] Priya: Yes, you can mark labels as immutable for evals.
[05:52] Tara: Security question - SSO, RBAC, audit logs?
[05:56] Maya: We support SAML/SSO, role-based access, and full audit trails. For Private, we can forward logs into your SIEM.
[06:04] Evan: Any competitors we should worry about for this use case?
[06:07] Maya: Customers often look at Anthropic and OpenAI for model capabilities; for managed eval pipelines some teams try to DIY with internal infra or Vertex AI. We position on operational depth for inference and cost controls.
[06:18] Jenna: Show a regression alert scenario again - maybe simulate a paraphrase that trips the system.
[06:22] Liam: Good idea. I'll run a paraphrase-heavy batch and we can watch thresholds. (typing) Ok run started. You can see a live chart of metric deltas and per-prompt failures.
[06:40] [00:06:40] Speaker 2: some transcripts are a little noisy - the auto-transcribe shows K-V cash instead of KV cache.
[06:46] Samir: ha, yeah the transcript won't be perfect.
[06:50] Priya: The UI allows you to open a failing prompt and see model outputs side-by-side A vs B. You can also flag examples for re-labeling.
[07:00] Jenna: If we flag examples, can those be used to auto-trigger a retrain or a fine-tune?
[07:04] Liam: Not automatically in the basic EvalOps flow, but you can wire an action to enqueue a retrain job. We can help set that up for the pilot.
[07:12] Samir: We definitely want a workflow to triage, label, and iterate.
[07:15] Maya: That's a common pattern. We'll include a runbook sample.
[07:20] Evan: For model variants, how strict is deterministic routing? We need sticky sessions for stateful interactions.
[07:25] Liam: Sticky routing for session-based KV cache is supported. For longer chats, the runtime maintains KV caches and we can pin sessions to a model variant.
[07:33] Tara: Any pen tests or compliance attestations you can share?
[07:36] Maya: We'll attach our pen test summary and SOC2 report. For more sensitive customers we can run an on-site or third-party audit.
[07:45] Samir: Ok lets talk timeline again: pilot scope is 2 weeks of daily regression runs against ~2k prompt seeds, A/B live split on 5% traffic to start, and report back with signal and cost. Does that fit?
[07:58] Liam: Yes, technically straightforward. We'll need infra contacts to set up VPC peering if you pick Private, else hosted onboarding is much faster.
[08:08] Jenna: What about pupp... sorry, public cloud region? We need EU hosting for some user segments.
[08:12] Maya: We have EU regions and can route traffic by region. For residency we can keep logs in-region for EU tenants.
[08:20] Evan: Anything about latency? If we route to quantized 13B the tail latency might increase.
[08:24] Liam: We optimize kernels and batching; for real-time triage we can keep smaller models for low latency and route complex cases to bigger models async. That's a cost-quality tradeoff we can help model.
[08:36] [00:08:36] Speaker 1: demo showing A/B side-by-side outputs, mark as pass/fail, open the alert playbook.
[08:50] Priya: Also note the ranking/weighting UI for composite metrics; you can tune recall weight high.
[09:00] Samir: For the pilot we want an initial set of 2k prompts picked from logs, and 500 clinician-labeled gold examples.
[09:06] Maya: Sounds good. We'll propose sample extraction queries and a sampling plan.
[09:12] Tara: One more security nit - do you have a contract appendix for data residency and breach notification windows?
[09:18] Maya: Yes, we'll include a standard DPA and we can add a residency appendix.
[09:22] Evan: Ok last: can we get sample API calls for programmatic creation of A/B runs?
[09:26] Liam: Yes - example in the SDK: createPromptSet, uploadGoldLabels, createEvaluationRun({candidates:["model-a","model-b"], metrics:["recall_on_red_flags"], split:{type:"live",percent:5}}) and webhook config. We'll share a gist.
[09:44] [00:09:44] Speaker 2: brief cross-talk about budgets - numbers will come via the spreadsheet.
[09:55] Priya: Demo wrap-up: here's how a typical incident would be handled: alert->triage->label->A/B run->rollback.
[10:05] Samir: That flow looks ok. Who will be our main contacts?
[10:08] Maya: I'll be the AE contact, Liam is your SE, Priya is product for setup.
[10:12] Jenna: Great. Any blockers on Redwood side to run pilot?
[10:16] Liam: Just contract and basic account provisioning; if you pick private we'll need networking info.
[10:22] Tara: We'll review the DPA and KMS requirements first.
[10:26] Maya: Alright quick recap and next steps - we'll send SOW + pricing, SOC2 & pen test, sample prompt CSV and sampling queries, and set up a kickoff call next week.
[10:40] Samir: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[10:43] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up.

End of transcript

Notes: transcript contains some auto-transcription artifacts (e.g., K-V cash), some speaker attributions may be generic. Shared links during call: link to pilot SOW (TBD), link to EvalOps API gist (TBD), benchmark spreadsheet (TBD).
